title: Erlang Examples
description: Each example belongs to one starter lesson. Follow its setup steps before trying it. These examples need the named tools and do not run in this site playground.

examples.title: Print a greeting
examples.description: io:format writes output. ~n starts a new line. The module exports main so the command can call it.

examples.title: Bind one value
examples.description: Variables start with a capital letter. A variable can be bound only once in a function call.

examples.title: Use a named label
examples.description: Atoms are fixed labels. An unquoted atom usually starts with a lower-case letter.

examples.title: Group a few values
examples.description: A tuple can hold a status and a result. Pattern matching pulls its parts into names.

examples.title: Split a list
examples.description: [Head | Tail] separates the first item from the rest of a list.

examples.title: Read a named key
examples.description: A map keeps key-value pairs. maps:get reads the value for a key.
examples.code:
-module(lesson).
-export([main/0]).
main() ->
    Book = #{title => "Moon Trip", pages => 24},
    io:format("~s~n", [maps:get(title, Book)]).

examples.title: Choose from patterns
examples.description: case compares a value with patterns. The first matching branch supplies the result.
examples.code:
-module(lesson).
-export([main/0]).
main() ->
    Light = green,
    Message = case Light of red -> "Stop"; green -> "Go"; _ -> "Wait" end,
    io:format("~s~n", [Message]).

examples.title: Check a number in a branch
examples.description: A guard adds a small test after a pattern. when introduces that test.
examples.code:
-module(lesson).
-export([main/0]).
main() ->
    Score = 8,
    Message = case Score of N when N >= 5 -> "Pass"; _ -> "Try again" end,
    io:format("~s~n", [Message]).

examples.title: Call a local function
examples.description: A named function can take an input and return its final expression.

examples.title: Make a list by a rule
examples.description: A list comprehension visits values and builds a result for each one.

examples.title: Send a message
examples.description: A process has a mailbox. ! sends a message, and receive reads a matching message.
examples.code:
-module(lesson).
-export([main/0]).
main() ->
    self() ! {score, 8},
    receive {score, N} -> io:format("~p~n", [N]) end.

examples.title: Start a small process
examples.description: spawn starts a new process. It can send a result back to the parent process.
examples.code:
-module(lesson).
-export([main/0]).
main() ->
    Parent = self(),
    spawn(fun() -> Parent ! {answer, 4 * 2} end),
    receive {answer, N} -> io:format("~p~n", [N]) end.
